[EFFECT] Year acts as a simple step change: 2011 (yr = 0) consistently pulls demand down (contribution clustered around −0.25 to −0.30), while 2012 (yr = 1) consistently pushes it up (clustered around +0.15 to +0.25). The model learned that the second year had systematically higher overall demand.
[IMPORTANCE] This is a moderate-importance feature with a vertical range of roughly 0.6–0.7 log-units, placing it toward the lower-middle of the ranking.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your staffing and bike availability primarily around the hour of the day — the evening peak (around 5–6 pm) and the morning shoulder (around 8 am) drive the largest swings in demand — and use temperature as the key weather signal, targeting comfortable mild days (~20–25 °C) for maximum expected ridership and scaling back during cold or very hot spells.
